sections.title: Market Pulse: Tech Sell-off and Fed Watch Define Trading Day

items.headline: U.S. Equities Decline Amid Tech Weakness and Anticipation of Fed Decision
items.summary: U.S. stock markets ended lower today, primarily driven by a continued sell-off in the technology and semiconductor sectors, coupled with investor caution ahead of the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East further fueled volatility and pushed oil prices higher, adding to inflation concerns. Not financial advice.

items.statContext: Closed lower today, extending recent declines amid tech sector weakness.
Underperformed as chip and technology stocks faced significant selling pressure.
Fell today as investors rotated out of growth stocks into more defensive assets.

items.headline: Sherwin-Williams Jumps on Strong Earnings
items.summary: Shares of $SHW climbed 8.3% to $3.7 after the company reported better-than-expected second-quarter 2026 earnings, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate.

items.headline: Cognizant Technology Solutions Rises on Revenue Growth
items.summary: $CTSH gained 7.7% today, fueled by robust second-quarter revenue growth and strong performance in its financial services segment, alongside expanding artificial intelligence partnerships.

items.headline: Ford Motor Co. Surges After Earnings Beat
items.summary: $F climbed 5.6% following a strong second-quarter earnings beat and an upward revision of its full-year profit and cash flow guidance.

items.headline: SanDisk Plunges as Chip Sector Faces Pressure
items.summary: SanDisk ($SNDK) experienced a significant drop of 13.33% to $1,107.84, shedding $170.39 during the session, as the semiconductor sector continues to face heavy selling pressure and profit-taking.

items.headline: Coherent Declines Amid Tech Sector Weakness
items.summary: Coherent ($COHR) declined 12.58% to $237.18, losing $34.13, reflecting broader weakness in technology and semiconductor stocks.

items.headline: V.F. Corp. Misses Earnings Expectations
items.summary: V.F. Corp. ($VFC) fell 17.64% to $15.03 after reporting its first earnings miss in the last four quarters, with results below analyst expectations.

sections.title: Sector Analysis: Tech and Energy Lag, Staples and Healthcare Lead Rotation

items.headline: Technology and Semiconductor Sectors Under Severe Pressure
items.summary: The technology and semiconductor sectors were significant laggards today, continuing a trend of 'risk-off' rotation. Investors pulled capital from high-multiple AI infrastructure stocks, leading to sharp declines across chipmakers and data infrastructure companies.

items.headline: Defensive Sectors Gain as Market Rotates
items.summary: In a notable sector rotation, defensive segments such as healthcare and consumer staples showed strength. These sectors saw increased buying interest as investors sought refuge from the volatility in growth-oriented technology stocks.

items.headline: Energy Sector Sees Volatility Amid Geopolitical Events
items.summary: The energy sector experienced significant price swings, largely driven by escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. While some energy stocks benefited from rising crude oil prices, the overall sentiment remained cautious due to global supply concerns.

items.headline: Federal Reserve Holds Rates Steady, Eyes Inflation
items.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) concluded its meeting today, maintaining the benchmark interest rate in the range of 3.50% to 3.75%. While the decision was widely anticipated, Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference was closely watched for clues on future monetary policy, particularly given persistent inflation concerns and rising oil prices.

items.headline: Q2 Earnings Season Continues with Mixed Results
items.summary: The second-quarter earnings season gained momentum with several major companies reporting. Humana ($HUM), Biogen ($BIIB), and General Dynamics ($GD) posted strong results, while V.F. Corp. ($VFC) missed expectations. Post-market, Microsoft ($MSFT) and Meta Platforms ($META) are among the tech giants releasing their earnings reports, with investors scrutinizing their AI investment returns.

items.headline: Geopolitical Tensions Drive Oil Prices Higher
items.summary: Escalating hostilities in the Middle East, including U.S. and Saudi Arabian strikes against Iran-backed forces, pushed Brent crude oil prices up by 5.6% to $86.64 per barrel. This rise in energy costs is contributing to broader inflation concerns and influencing market sentiment.
